Strategy interface methods: we need a simple strategy that decides when to operate. We can implement a custom Strategy that returns true for entry/exit based on index parity.

Goal: test run method variations, ensure start/end indexes bounding, ensure that after run, tradingRecord contains expected trades.

Simplify: We'll create a basic BarSeries implementation with a list of bars (Bar interface not listed but needed for getBarData etc). BarSeriesManager.run iterates i from runBeginIndex to runEndIndex and calls strategy.shouldOperate(i, tradingRecord). The default implementation of shouldOperate in Strategy interface uses entry/exit rules; but we can provide our own implementation overriding shouldOperate to return true for specific indices.

Thus we can avoid dealing with Bar objects.

Implementation steps:

- Define SimpleNum implements Num with BigDecimal value, implement required methods minimally (only ones used: one() from factory returns SimpleNum.ONE; plus, minus, multipliedBy, dividedBy, isZero, intValue, longValue, doubleValue, etc). For simplicity we can delegate to BigDecimal and implement others as needed.

- Define SimpleNumFactory with method one() returning SimpleNum.ONE.

- SimpleBarSeries implements BarSeries: store beginIndex = 0, endIndex = size-1, barData list (empty). Provide numFactory returning SimpleNumFactory. getBeginIndex returns begin; getEndIndex returns end; getBarData returns list; other methods can throw UnsupportedOperationException or return default.

- SimpleTradeExecutionModel implements TradeExecutionModel: in execute, it will call tradingRecord.enter or exit based on tradeType? Actually tradingRecord is BaseTradingRecord with entry trade type predetermined. The execute method should simulate a trade: if there is no current position open, we call tradingRecord.operate(index). BaseTradingRecord.operate method will decide entry/exit automatically based on internal logic (calls enter/exit). But we don't know its behavior. Simpler: we'll just call tradingRecord.operate(index) which will cause entry/exit according to its own logic (but we need to set price and amount? operate(index) default uses price from barSeries? Not sure. BaseTradingRecord has operate(int index) default, which uses price from series? unknown. Safer: call tradingRecord.enter(index, amount, amount) maybe. But we can just call tradingRecord.operate(index) and rely that it registers a trade.

Thus SimpleTradeExecutionModel execute will call tradingRecord.operate(index). That's enough.

Then run with a strategy that returns true at first index only. Expect tradingRecord to have a position opened and maybe closed depending on later calls.

Simplify: Strategy that always returns true for shouldOperate, causing execute each index. Our execute will call tradingRecord.operate each time; BaseTradingRecord will have logic to open and close alternating? Not sure. To make deterministic, we can implement a custom TradingRecord? Not allowed to subclass. But we can use BaseTradingRecord directly. It will treat operate as entry if no open position else exit. So first call opens, second call closes, third opens, etc. So after run over 3 indices, we expect 2 trades (entry+exit) and one open position? Actually three operations: open at i0, close at i1, open at i2 (open). So final position open. isClosed false.

Thus test verify.

Edge cases: test run with startIndex > series begin, and finishIndex beyond end, ensuring bounds.

Also test that if last position open and runEndIndex == series end, manager will attempt to close after series end using extra loop. We'll need to have series with 2 bars, runEndIndex = end, and strategy should operate on next index (i=2) to close. Since our SimpleTradeExecutionModel will operate on that index, the position should close.

Implementation details: Need to know series size for extra loop. SimpleBarSeries getBarData size maybe 2. getEndIndex = size-1 = 1. After run, for i from runEndIndex+1 to seriesMaxSize-1 (seriesMaxSize = max(endIndex+1, barData.size()) = max(2,2)=2) => loop runs for i=2? No, i < seriesMaxSize, so i=2 is not <2, loop not executed. So to test extra loop, we need seriesMaxSize > endIndex+1. That requires barData.size() > endIndex+1. But endIndex = series.getEndIndex() = size-1, so size == endIndex+1. So seriesMaxSize equals that. So extra loop never runs. Actually comment says "if there are still bars after the endIndex of the barSeries, then we execute the strategy on these bars". But since endIndex is last bar, there are none. So we cannot test that scenario unless we artificially set finishIndex less than series end, then after run, if position open and runEndIndex == series.getEndIndex()? Wait condition: if (!tradingRecord.isClosed() && runEndIndex == barSeries.getEndIndex()) then loop over extra bars beyond series end (but there are none). So not testable. Maybe we can set series with extra dummy bars beyond getBarData size? Not possible.

Thus test main functionality.

Implement SimpleNum with static ONE.

Implement SimpleNumFactory with one().

Implement SimpleBarSeries with getBeginIndex returns 0, getEndIndex returns data.size()-1.

Implement SimpleStrategy implements Strategy: store set of indices where shouldOperate true. Implement shouldOperate to return indicesSet.contains(index). Provide other methods as default (maybe return null for others). Must implement getName, getEntryRule, getExitRule, etc. Since default methods rely on those, but we override shouldOperate, we can leave others returning null.

Implement SimpleTradeExecutionModel with execute: tradingRecord.operate(index);

Get TradingRecord. Verify trade count = 3? Actually each operate creates a trade (entry or exit). BaseTradingRecord stores trades list with each trade (entry and exit). After 3 operations: entry at 0, exit at 1, entry at 2. So trades size = 3. Positions count = 2 (first closed, second open). isClosed false.

- testRunWithStartAndFinishIndices: run with start=1 finish=2. Expect operations only for indices 1 and 2. Verify trades size = 2 (entry at 1, exit at 2). isClosed true.
